output.text: In the quiet hush of a workshop lit by dawn’s pale glow, a hand lifts a dry stick of ink. It is ancient, dense—born of soot and time. The maker lowers it into the black pool, a stillness waiting to be stirred. One drop at a time, water is added, each drop a breath, a pause, a memory. The ink stirs, deepens, begins to live. Then, the brush touches rice paper—thin, porous, alive. A line begins, hesitant, then sure. It flows, unbroken, across the surface. And as it travels, it grows—not just in length, but in meaning. A line becomes a river. The ink, once dry, now speaks. It remembers every drop, every moment, every silence between them.
